Let \(\alpha=\angle ACB\), \(\beta=\angle ABC\), and let \(R\) be the circumradius.  
Since \(I\) is the incenter,
\[
CI=\frac{r}{\sin(\alpha/2)}.
\]
Also \(r=4R\sin\frac A2\sin\frac B2\sin\frac C2\), so
\[
CI=4R\sin\frac A2\sin\frac{\beta}{2}.
\]
Given \(AB=AC+CI\), and using \(AB=2R\sin\alpha,\ AC=2R\sin\beta\),
\[
2R\sin\alpha=2R\sin\beta+4R\sin\frac A2\sin\frac{\beta}{2}.
\]
Thus
\[
\sin\alpha-\sin\beta=2\sin\frac A2\sin\frac{\beta}{2}.
\]
Since \(A=\pi-\alpha-\beta\), we have \(\sin\frac A2=\cos\frac{\alpha+\beta}{2}\). Hence
\[
2\cos\frac{\alpha+\beta}{2}\sin\frac{\alpha-\beta}{2}
=
2\cos\frac{\alpha+\beta}{2}\sin\frac{\beta}{2}.
\]
Canceling the positive cosine,
\[
\sin\frac{\alpha-\beta}{2}=\sin\frac{\beta}{2}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\frac{\alpha-\beta}{2}=\frac{\beta}{2},
\]
so \(\alpha=2\beta\). Thus
\[
\frac{\angle ACB}{\angle ABC}=\frac{\alpha}{\beta}=2.
\]

\[
\boxed{2}
\]
